title: Day Three Hundred Sixty-Six
subject: a man whose kettle dies on day 366 of its one-year warranty, who storms the electrical shop with the receipt and a calendar, and is offered ten percent off a new kettle
caption: Bay Area thrash metal, mid-80s style. Two palm-muted downpicked electric guitars playing fast chugging riffs, an overdriven bass locked to them, galloping double-kick drums with a cracking snare, one short shredded guitar solo. Tight dry 80s thrash production with scooped mids. Male lead in a barked mid-range thrash shout with clear diction, gang shouts on the hook. 184 BPM, E minor. Furious, ridiculous and righteous. No nu-metal rap, no deathcore growls or breakdowns, no autotune, no pop chorus, no symphonic keys.
lyrics:
[Intro - galloping riff and double kick]

[Verse 1]
Morning brew, I flick the switch
Not a spark and not a hiss
Turn the box, the sticker reads
One year cover, guaranteed

[Pre-Chorus]
Count the days on the calendar
Three six six, one day too far

[Chorus]
Day three hundred sixty-six
Kettle dead and nothing fixed
Day three hundred sixty-six
Leap year, mate, I know your tricks

[Verse 2]
Down the high street, receipt in hand
Kettle tucked beneath my arm
Lad in blue just shakes his head
Should have died a day ahead

[Chorus]
Day three hundred sixty-six
Policy says no to this
Day three hundred sixty-six
Small print says you take the hit

[Bridge - guitar solo]

[Chorus]
Day three hundred sixty-six
Ten percent off, that's the fix
Day three hundred sixty-six
Boil it in a pan, that's it

[Outro - final riff and stop]
New kettle, same brand, same shop
Mark the date and watch the clock
